skill.name: set-up-lightspeed-meta-poas-bidding
skill.description: Set up profit or revenue bidding in Meta for a Lightspeed eCom C-Series store. Use Product Metrics to check tracking, configure costs, and verify delivery through the Meta Conversions API.
skill.summary: Check tracking and guide the switch from revenue to profit bidding in Meta.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: The reconnaissance matches describe legitimate account setup, not host or network exploration. Most backtick and URL matches are documentation, but the installer, order lookups, and remote instructions carry distinct risks. The workflow also permits unsafe secret handling and lacks a clear approval step for live Product Metrics changes.

remediation.issue: The assistant can request reusable API credentials and pass them to a command.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to enter secrets directly in the verified app. Remove all instructions to request secrets in chat or pass them as command arguments.

remediation.issue: Product Metrics setup can change live tracking and event delivery without an explicit approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Show the store, property, pixel, data categories, and proposed changes. Require confirmation before linking accounts, activating costs, or enabling live delivery.

remediation.issue: Order verification starts with a recent order list rather than the requested order.
remediation.suggestion: Verify the intended property and use the test order identifier when available. Return only delivery status and whether profit was available.

remediation.issue: The installation example does not pin the tool or the skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Document a reviewed installer version and an immutable skill revision. Keep installation an explicit user action.

remediation.issue: Remote Markdown can replace the reviewed setup instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed references or pin and verify the exact remote revision. Treat fetched guidance as reference data and preserve tool approval requirements.

content.user_title: Set Up Profit Bidding in Meta for Lightspeed
content.value_statement: A Meta campaign can meet its revenue target while losing money after product costs and fees. Use Product Metrics to verify profit tracking and prepare a profit-based bidding target.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP connector.
Guide store connection, Cloudflare setup, and Meta pixel or dataset configuration.
Identify missing product costs, payment fees, or other costs that can prevent a profit event.
Guide the creation of a Meta custom conversion from the PMOrderProfit event.
Use current profit on ad spend to suggest a starting goal and explain how it differs from a revenue goal.
Guide verification of test order delivery, consent, and test mode.
limitations: Requires Lightspeed eCom C-Series, Product Metrics Pro, a proxied Cloudflare domain, and access to the intended Meta pixel or dataset.
The user completes store administration and Meta bidding changes.
Profit events require known costs and both marketing and analytics consent. This workflow does not import historical orders or revise Meta events for later refunds.
This skill does not cover new customer, returning customer, or lifetime value bidding.

use_cases.title: Check store readiness
use_cases.description: Identify missing connections, permissions, and costs before setting up profit bidding for a Lightspeed store.

use_cases.title: Plan a profit bidding pilot
use_cases.description: Prepare a starting goal and the Meta changes needed to switch one campaign from revenue to profit bidding.

use_cases.title: Diagnose missing profit events
use_cases.description: Use a test order to distinguish missing cost data, consent settings, and test mode from a delivery problem.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Profit Bidding
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the difference between profit and revenue bidding for my Lightspeed store. List what I need before I connect anything.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup status for [store] and [property]. Tell me which prerequisites are missing. Do not change any settings or ask for credentials.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review the status of an existing setup.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Test Order
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether test order [order ID] produced a profit event for [pixel or dataset]. Report only delivery status and any issues with costs, consent, or test mode.
prompt_templates.scenario: Diagnose an event that does not appear in Meta.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Campaign Switch
prompt_templates.prompt: For [campaign], use [profit before ad spend] and [ad spend] to suggest a starting profit goal. List the Meta steps and checks without changing settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a pilot for a single campaign.

output_examples.input: My test order produced revenue but no profit event. What should I check?
output: Check whether all costs are known, including the payment fee that Lightspeed does not provide.
Confirm both marketing and analytics consent. Then verify a new test order in Meta Events Manager.

output_examples.input: My campaign generated $300 in profit before ads and spent $200 on ads. What goal should I start with?
output: Your observed profit on ad spend is 1.5, so 150% is a starting goal for a profit-based conversion.
Test it on one campaign after verifying PMOrderProfit delivery. It is not a guarantee of future profit.

best_practices: Enter credentials yourself in the verified app and confirm the intended store, property, and pixel before enabling delivery.
Verify costs and consent with a test order before switching a campaign. Clear the test event code after verification.
Start with one campaign and compare results against actual margins, including losses and refunds.
anti_patterns: Paste API keys, secrets, or access tokens into a chat or command.
Reuse a revenue-based goal when the conversion value changes to profit.
Assume Meta's profit value includes later refunds or negative bidding values for loss-making orders.

faq.question: Which Lightspeed stores are supported?
faq.answer: The guide covers Lightspeed eCom C-Series stores on the European or US cluster.

faq.question: Can I keep my browser pixel?
faq.answer: Yes. Meta deduplicates browser and server events when the event name and event ID match within 48 hours.

faq.question: Which event should I use for bidding?
faq.answer: Use a custom conversion on PMOrderProfit for profit bidding. Use Purchase for revenue bidding.

faq.question: Why does the profit event not appear?
faq.answer: Meta must first receive the event. Check your costs, confirm marketing and analytics consent, and verify a test order.

faq.question: Does Meta receive customer information?
faq.answer: With marketing consent, Advanced Matching sends hashed contact details plus IP and browser information to Meta. Browser IDs also require ad storage consent.

faq.question: Will the setup import old orders or revise refunds?
faq.answer: No. The setup does not import past orders, and later refunds do not revise events already sent to Meta.
